## One site model (G19, v4.15)
Per site, once a week: the **canonical host** (the homepage as a browser gets it, redirects followed, plus its `rel=canonical` and the site's own live URLs), the business **name / logo / NAP** (`seo_profiles` -> the homepage Organization / LocalBusiness schema -> Google Business Profile -> the app's fields), the **services**, the **nav pages**, the business facts, the brand names and the competitors (`seo_monitors`). *Site Metrics* merges `SM.toRow(model)` into the `seo_sites` row, so every workflow reads the same facts; a model younger than 7 days is kept and no request is made. The page inventory lives in `seo_pages` (D11). Kit: `v5/code/_site_model.js`, spec: `SITE_MODEL_SPEC.md`.

## Publish detection (v4.8)
Before the Google part, per site with pages **written but not published** (`seo_content_log` status started, no URL, last 120 days; `seo_ladders` status writing): `/sitemap.xml` is read (an index: its 5 newest child sitemaps) and every URL compared host-agnostically — **slug** (planned path / planned slug / keyword slug) first, then for up to 10 unmatched pages the **title / first H1** of up to 15 pages per site whose slug holds 60%+ of the keyword's words (80%+ needed in the title or H1). A page improving an existing URL counts when its sitemap `lastmod` is after it was written. Found pages are stored like "I published a page" (content log + ladder row + case study), inspected in Search Console in this run, and listed in the report and the callback (`detected_published`). Plain HTTP, no paid call; no waiting page = no request.

parameters.text:
=You are a senior SEO analyst writing the weekly performance brief for one website. You receive computed FACTS (JSON) for the last 28 days against the 28 days before: Search Console totals and deltas, query and page movers, striking-distance queries (positions 4-20 with impressions), CTR gaps, decaying pages, the tracked keywords, the index status of the planned "ladder" pages, GA4 organic traffic and Google Trends.
Write for the site owner: busy, not an SEO specialist, wants to know what changed, why it matters and what to do.

Rules
- Every statement must come from the facts; quote the numbers (clicks, impressions, positions, percentages, page paths). Never invent a figure or a page.
- British spelling. Plain words. No praise, no filler, no generic advice ("create quality content").
- facts.website is the site model every part of the agent uses: call the business by facts.website.business_name and write every URL of this site on facts.website.canonical_host (https). Never use the bare domain when the canonical host is the www one, and never invent a name.
- If Search Console or GA4 is not connected, say so in one line and work with what exists (tracked keywords, live checks, trends); the headline must then be about connecting Google.
- actions: at most 5, ordered by expected impact, each concrete: which page or query, what to change, the expected effect. Prefer the computed_actions but reword them for the owner and merge duplicates. Use "keyword" and "url" fields when the action is about one query or one page.
- Ladder pages with status "planned" or "writing" are not on the site yet: say they are not published yet, never that they are "not indexed".
- The site already has pages (facts.website.pages_known). When a computed action is of type "refresh_existing", a live page already answers that search: say to refresh that exact page (name its URL), never to publish a second page for the same search — two pages for one search split the signals and neither ranks.
- Google Trends: a trend whose direction is "sparse", or that carries "change" instead of "change_pct", has too little search data — say "too little search data" for it and never quote a percentage or call it rising or falling.
- An alert or a change that the facts mark as not statistically significant ("watch") is a thing to watch, not a fall: say so in those words and never quote it as a confirmed drop.
- A manual action or security issue (from a Search Console notice or the monthly check-in) is always the first action and the headline.
- highlights: 2-4 one-line facts worth remembering (biggest win, biggest loss, best opportunity, index status).
- watch: 0-3 things to re-check next week (a page that dropped, a keyword slipping, a trend turning).
- Keep the summary to 3-4 sentences.

Return JSON only: {"headline": "...", "summary": "...", "highlights": ["...", "..."], "actions": [{"priority": 1, "action": "...", "why": "...", "keyword": "", "url": ""}], "watch": ["..."]}

FACTS
{{ $json.facts }}

// Copy of each report HTML named index.html for the PDF renderer (Gotenberg requires that exact file name); one item per site.
return $input.all().map(item => { const doc = (item.binary || {}).data; if (!doc) return item; return { json: item.json, binary: { data: doc, html: { ...doc, fileName: 'index.html', mimeType: 'text/html', fileExtension: 'html' } } }; });

parameters.content:
## SEO Agent — Site Tracker (v4.3)
Runs **every Monday 09:00** (after the Rank Tracker) and on demand through *Manual Run* (`{ site_id | domain, on_demand: true }`; the main workflow calls it right after "Track my site"). Sites come from the Data Table `seo_sites` plus every domain with a keyword ladder (tracked automatically). All tables are created on first use.
**Google (free, service account):** `GSC Sites` finds the Search Console property the service account can read (sc-domain first) → Search Analytics for the last 28 complete days vs the 28 before and the same period a year ago (totals by day, top queries with page, pages, each tracked keyword as an exact query) → **URL Inspection** of the ladder pages (indexed?). GA4: property id from the registration or **detected** from the web stream URL (`GA4 Accounts` → `GA4 Streams`) → organic channel totals, organic landing pages, organic sessions by day.
**Paid (DataForSEO):** Google Trends for up to 4 head terms per site ($0.011 each, measured) and a live top-50 check for the site's own keywords (~$0.015 each, max 20; ladder keywords are read from the Rank Tracker's history).
**Site Metrics** computes deltas, winners/losers/new/lost queries, striking-distance queries (4-20), CTR gaps, decaying pages, index status, alerts and ranked actions with API bodies; rows go to `seo_site_metrics` (one row per site per run), `seo_query_history` (tracked keywords + top 100 queries), `seo_trends` (for the Content Cadence) and back into `seo_sites`. Pages written by the Content Cadence (`seo_content_log`) are tracked as "blog" keywords; published ones are inspected; pages without a publish link are listed as waiting — or, since v4.8, found live through the sitemap and recorded automatically (*Publish detection*, the nodes above). Search Console **notices** (`seo_console_alerts`, from the Console Alerts mail watcher and the monthly check-in) and the latest **check-in** (`seo_console_checkins`) appear as alerts, actions and a report section; a missing check-in for the month is reminded every Monday. **Site Brief** (Claude Sonnet 5.5, ~$0.03 per site) words the week for the owner; **Site Report** builds the e-mail (KPI tiles, actions, tracked keywords, ladder index status, movers, opportunities, traffic, trends) + PDF; delivery by e-mail and/or callback (`stage: site_tracker`).
Credential **Google Service Account (SEO Agent)** (`googleApi`, "Set up for use in HTTP Request node" on, scopes `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly`). The owner adds the service-account e-mail to Search Console (Full) and GA4 (Viewer); put that e-mail into `CONFIG.service_account_email` in *Site Plan* so the connect instructions name it. Not connected = the report still runs (trends, live checks) and explains the two steps.
Form: http://localhost:5678/form/54f85234-172e-43e6-a84d-b5ecaa140e7d · API: http://localhost:5678/webhook/seo-keyword-check (`mode: track`)
